design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that participants were randomly assigned to cognitive-processing therapy, prolonged exposure, or minimal attention, although the sequence-generation and concealment procedures are not described.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were explicitly randomly assigned and reported baseline characteristics and pretreatment outcomes were balanced, but the sequence-generation method and allocation concealment were not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The design of the project involved random assignment of participants to CPT, PE, or MA.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and therapists necessarily knew the behavioral treatment received, but treatment fidelity was closely supervised, adherence was high, therapist assignment was balanced, and ITT analyses were reported; nevertheless, LOCF was used and post-randomization exclusions occurred.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Throughout the study, all of the sessions were videotaped, and therapy was closely supervised by the principal investigator, with weekly peer-supervision sessions to ensure competence and adherence to the protocols.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were not collected after treatment dropout, attrition was substantial and differed between active treatment and minimal-attention groups, and LOCF or model-based analyses cannot exclude bias from outcome-dependent missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Therefore, we did not continue to assess women who dropped out of treatment, and we administered only one scale, the PSS, during treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The main outcomes were measured with validated clinician-administered and self-report instruments using common procedures across groups, assessments were described as independent, and interviewer reliability was actively monitored.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Independent assessments were made at pretreatment, posttreatment, and 3 and 9 months posttreatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prespecified protocol or analysis plan is reported, multiple outcomes and analytic populations/methods were examined, and outcome collection and follow-up timing were changed after the trial began, creating substantial scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Once the study started, a 9-month follow-up was added.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because participants who discontinued treatment were not followed for most outcomes, producing substantial missing data handled partly by LOCF, and because the unregistered study used multiple outcomes and analyses while changing follow-up and measurement plans after initiation. Randomization and outcome measurement were otherwise reasonably supportive, but allocation concealment was not reported.

design_rationale: Participants at each site were explicitly randomly assigned to PE, PE/CR, or wait-list, with the study statistician using a weighted randomization procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: Assignment was performed by the study statistician using weighted randomization, but the method used to generate the random sequence and allocation concealment before assignment were not reported, and baseline PSS-I severity differed between PE/CR and PE.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study statistician assigned participants who provided informed consent to one of the three conditions using a weighted randomization procedure such that participants were assigned to one of the active treatment conditions at a greater rate than to WL.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and therapists necessarily knew the assigned behavioral treatment, treatment duration was response-adaptive, and 11 randomized participants were excluded from the stated intent-to-treat sample, although fidelity was high and analyses otherwise included dropouts with imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thus, our intent-to-treat sample consisted of 179 women who signed consent, were randomized to a condition, and were not removed by the investigators.

domain_judgments.rationale: Posttreatment attrition was large and markedly differential between active treatment and wait-list groups, and replacing missing posttreatment outcomes with baseline scores is an unsupported single-imputation approach that can bias treatment-effect estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The overall dropout rate was 32.4% and was lower for WL (3.8%) than PE/CR (40.5%)... and PE (34.2%)... [analyses] substituting pretreatment scores for missing posttreatment scores.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary PTSD outcome was measured with a validated semistructured interview administered consistently by trained evaluators blinded to condition, with strong interrater reliability and explicit precautions against unblinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All evaluations were conducted by trained doctoral or master’s level CTSA clinicians who were blind to study condition... Participants were instructed by their therapists and the evaluators to not reveal any information that might unblind the evaluator to treatment condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and several outcomes, analysis populations, time points, and analytic contrasts created scope for selective reporting, although the named primary outcome and major planned comparisons were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We conducted separate Group (WL vs. PE/CR vs. PE) × Site (CTSA vs. WOAR) × Time (pre- vs. posttreatment) mixed factorial ANOVAs on the PSS–I, BDI, SAS–W, and SAS–S scores for the intent-to-treat sample.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because substantial, differential attrition across randomized groups was handled by baseline-score substitution, leaving a high risk that missing outcome data biased the effect estimates. Additional concerns arise from incomplete reporting of sequence generation/concealment, postrandomization exclusions, and lack of a reported prespecified analysis plan.

design_rationale: The 153 participants were explicitly randomized by computerized software after baseline, using a concealed computer-held sequence that mimicked a coin flip and balanced assignment over time.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was generated and concealed within the computerized software, and the modest baseline difference in number of risks was explicitly tested and was compatible with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After completion of the baseline assessment, the (computer) narrator “flipped a coin” and women (N=153) were randomized into the control or SHE intervention. The randomization sequence was known only to the computer program and optimized for balanced assignment over time between the two conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they received the computerized modules, but no intervention-related deviations were reported, both groups had equivalent access to referral assistance, and analyses used the full intention-to-treat sample.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All analyses use the full intent-to-treat sample.

domain_judgments.rationale: Chart-reviewed treatment utilization was available for all 153 participants, but self-reported treatment use and health-risk outcomes had appreciable and somewhat variable follow-up missingness, with no sensitivity analysis or evidence that missingness was unrelated to outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: participants in SHE compared to those in control were more likely to have higher levels of treatment as assessed by both chart review (χ2 (1, n = 153) = 4.38, p = .036... and self-report (χ2 (1, n = 130) = 5.89, p = .015...)

domain_judgments.rationale: The measures were appropriate and applied similarly across groups, with chart review providing an objective source, but blinding of chart abstractors was not reported and self-reported outcomes could be influenced by participants' knowledge of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment initiation and utilization were measured via self-report and chart review.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and primary and secondary outcomes were reportedly prespecified, but the authors reported numerous time points, measurement sources, and adjusted and unadjusted analyses, acknowledge multiplicity, and the supplied report does not establish a prespecified analysis plan for all choices.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Although we pre-specified our primary and secondary outcomes, the total number of analyses reported for number of health risks and treatment use (including both chart review and self-report) was large given that we examined health risks at both 2 and 4 months and presented both unadjusted and adjusted treatment effects for all outcomes. Thus, there was some inflation of type I error risk due to this multiple testing.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Randomization and intention-to-treat analysis were sound, and the principal chart-review treatment-use outcome was complete, but incomplete self-reported follow-up data, unreported assessor blinding, and analysis/reporting multiplicity raise concerns without clear evidence of severe bias.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 60 eligible participants were randomly assigned to M-CET or the wait-list control condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment was stated and baseline groups were broadly similar, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported, and there were chance-possible imbalances in trauma types.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible participants (n=60) were randomly assigned to either the control condition (n=31) or the treatment condition (n=29).

domain_judgments.rationale: Seven randomized treatment participants who attended no sessions were excluded from the stated intent-to-treat sample, reducing the treatment arm from 29 to 22, while the control condition also received supportive counseling; exclusion based on post-randomization intervention uptake could materially bias the effect estimate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: seven participants assigned to the treatment group were excluded from analyses because they did not attend a single treatment session.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was substantial (36.4% treatment and 25.8% control), and missing outcomes were handled using last observation carried forward, which does not establish that results were unbiased by missingness despite reported baseline similarity between completers and dropouts.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Missing data for individuals who dropped out of the study were imputed, using a last-value-carried-forward procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: Clinical assessments were performed by an independent evaluator blinded to condition and established measures were used, but several outcomes were self-reported by participants who necessarily knew whether they received therapy, and the PRS psychometric properties were still under investigation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All assessments were completed in person by an independent evaluator unaware of treatment condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, while numerous diagnostic, symptom, end-state, intent-to-treat, completer, and follow-up analyses provided substantial flexibility in selecting results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The dependent variables included diagnostic status based on the SCID and the CAPS, assessment of panic symptoms as measured by the ADIS, including number of full panic attacks in the previous month, fearfulness of panic attacks, and distress/interference from panic attacks.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by post-randomization exclusion of seven treatment-assigned participants from the purported intent-to-treat analysis and substantial attrition handled with last observation carried forward. Unreported allocation methods, unblinded self-reported outcomes, and lack of a reported prespecified analysis plan add further concerns.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that eligible consenting participants were randomly assigned to PE, SIT, PE-SIT, or wait-list control.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment was stated and baseline measures were broadly balanced, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported, and the allocation ratio was changed after 10 wait-list assignments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Those who met criteria for the study and signed consent forms were randomly assigned to one of the following four conditions: PE, SIT, combined treatment (PE–SIT), or WL. After enrolling 10 participants into WL, we assigned more participants to the three active groups than to WL.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and therapists necessarily knew the behavioral treatment received, and attrition differed by condition; adherence was high and an intent-to-treat analysis was reported, but last-value-carried-forward is not a robust method for preserving an unbiased treatment-effect estimate under differential dropout.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The dropout rate differed significantly across groups, χ2(3, N = 96) = 10.62, p < .025. More participants dropped out from SIT and PE–SIT (27%) than from the PE and WL conditions (5%)... We conducted... analyses on the intent-to-treat sample using a last-value-carried-forward procedure to impute missing data due to dropout.

domain_judgments.rationale: Posttreatment dropout was substantial and strongly differential across randomized groups, dropout outcome status was unknown, and the authors acknowledged that this could bias comparative efficacy; follow-up data were also incomplete and handled using simple imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We did not conduct assessments during the active-treatment phase and therefore do not have information on the status of dropouts at the time of termination... Because more participants dropped out from SIT and PE–SIT than from PE, this could have resulted in underestimating the efficacy of the former treatments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome instruments were established and independent evaluators were blinded to assignment, but self-reported outcomes could be influenced by participants' awareness of treatment and interrater reliability was not monitored systematically over the five-year study.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Independent evaluators were female clinicians with at least a master's degree who received extensive training in administration of the instruments and were unaware of treatment assignment... we did not evaluate interrater reliability systematically for the PSS–I, the SAS, and the SCID throughout the 5 years of this study, allowing for the possibility of rater drift.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan was reported, and numerous eligible outcomes, time points, populations, imputations, and analysis formulations were presented, permitting selective choice among results despite the stated primary hypotheses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The intent-to-treat analyses were followed by completer analyses... To evaluate the separate effects of PE and SIT, we conducted a series of 2 × 2 analyses on the posttreatment scores.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because missing outcome data were substantial, differed significantly by treatment group, and were handled with last-value-carried-forward despite unknown outcomes among dropouts. Additional concerns arise from unreported sequence concealment, participant awareness, possible rater drift, and analysis/reporting flexibility.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports individual allocation by an independent trial unit using a sequenced computer-generated randomization procedure with 1:1 allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although an independent unit generated the computer-randomized sequence and baseline values were similar, trial staff handled the envelopes and initially failed to use them in strict numerical order, so allocation concealment may have been compromised.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants received sequentially numbered trial materials with concealed allocation. Allocation envelopes were kept and handled by the trial staff. Due to initial misunderstandings, the prepared sealed envelopes were initially not always picked in strict numeric order.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and therapists necessarily knew allocation in this behavioral waitlist trial, which could influence behavior or expectations, although no intervention discontinuation occurred and the primary analysis was described as intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants could not be blinded to their treatment allocation due to the nature of this nonpharmacological intervention. Therapists involved in delivery of the intervention were also unblinded.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary follow-up data were missing for 3 of 36 participants (8.3%), and the ITT analysis used last-observation-carried-forward baseline values without evidence that missingness could not bias the result, although the amount of missingness was modest.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: When data was missing at time point two the last observation (baseline investigation data) was carried forward in the intention to treat analysis. Subjects with missing data (n = 3) were excluded in the per protocol analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was a subjective self-reported PTSD symptom scale, and participants were aware of receiving the novel psychotherapy or remaining on a waitlist, making differential expectancy and reporting effects likely; no blinded clinical assessment was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants could not be blinded to their treatment allocation due to the nature of this nonpharmacological intervention... Other limitations associated with resources were that... we relied on self-report data and self-rating rather than on clinical assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial stopped early after the research team conducted an unblinded, data-driven interim analysis showing a very large effect, despite an original target of 100 participants, creating substantial risk of selective timing and exaggerated effect estimates; prospective registration alone does not remove this concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The major differences between the groups at time point two in combination with lack of funding, led us to the decision to perform an interim analysis when 36 patients had completed the second measurement at time point two. An extremely large effect size... was found and the study was closed.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by unblinded measurement of a subjective self-reported outcome and unplanned, unblinded early stopping after observing a very large treatment effect. Additional concerns arise from imperfect envelope handling, lack of participant blinding, and baseline-value imputation for missing follow-up outcomes.

design_rationale: The 30 enrolled participants were explicitly assigned to RTM or waitlist using a pre-generated random-number list created independently with Microsoft Excel's random-number function.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was generated independently using a random-number function, but assignment by the site manager is not described in enough detail to establish allocation concealment, although reported baseline PTSD scores were broadly similar.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were admitted to the study in cohorts of 10 and randomly assigned to treatment or control groups by the site manager. This assignment was based on a list of random numbers, previously generated at an independent location using Microsoft Excel 2016’s random number function.

domain_judgments.rationale: The open-label waitlist design made participants and the sole therapist aware of treatment, concurrent medications and outside therapy were permitted, and the reported intention-to-treat analysis used potentially biased last/baseline observation carried forward rather than a more appropriate missing-data method.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: They, like experimental subjects, were not prohibited from continuing with other treatments, including medications... all computations were based on intent-to-treat analyses. Incomplete values were imputed using the last observation carried forward.

domain_judgments.rationale: For the randomized treatment-versus-waitlist comparison at study week 5, outcome data were essentially complete, with all 15 initially treated participants completing treatment and all controls reaching post-wait assessment; the single dropout occurred later during control participants' crossover treatment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All 15 individuals in the RTM group completed treatment. All 15 controls opted to receive treatment... One waitlist-control participant dropped out during treatment, citing family problems.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary short-term outcome was measured using an established structured PTSD interview administered consistently by independent assessors blinded to treatment condition, limiting differential measurement bias despite participants being unblinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Independent psychometricians, blinded to treatment condition, evaluated PTSD symptoms at intake, postwait (study week 5), and 2 weeks post. PSS-I and PCL-M were the primary and secondary measures of symptom severity.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective registration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, while multiple measures, thresholds, time points, symptom outcomes, and analyses were available; the investigators also used one-tailed tests and reported extremely small p-values, creating substantial scope for selective analysis and reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All significance testing used student’s independent t test, 1-tailed. All tests reported as p < .001, or “highly significant,” are in fact p < .000005.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because the absence of reported prospective registration or a prespecified analysis plan, together with numerous eligible outcomes and analyses and use of one-tailed testing, creates high risk of selective reporting. Additional concerns arise from unclear allocation concealment, the open-label waitlist design, concurrent treatments, and simplistic imputation, although short-term outcome completeness and blinded assessment were strengths.

design_rationale: Although the abstract says participants were randomly assigned, the Methods reports deterministic alternation by the order in which prescreening materials were returned, not a random allocation sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Deterministic alternation did not ensure exchangeability, important baseline differences existed in comorbidity and HRV, most participants received concurrent psychotherapy and medication, and the analyses did not adjust for these or other prognostic factors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The LZNF group reported a larger number of comorbid diagnoses at baseline (i.e., LZNF = 21, HRVB = 15)... The largest baseline differences were in the HRV measures, for which the LZNF group had higher initial levels.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were self-selected volunteers recruited through advertisements and enrolled first-come, first-served, while condition assignment depended on the timing of returned prescreening materials; however, assignment occurred after eligibility determination and consent, limiting evidence of direct outcome-related selection between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twenty-four eligible adults were enrolled on a firstcome, first-served basis and alternately assigned between the LZNF group and HRVB group according to the order in which they returned their prescreening materials.

domain_judgments.rationale: The two interventions were clearly defined, assigned before treatment, and delivered using distinct physiological signals and detailed standardized procedures, making misclassification unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All participants attended 15 sessions of the training to which they were assigned (i.e., LZNF or HRVB) at a rate of two sessions per week.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were aware of the intervention received, most continued outside psychotherapy and psychiatric medication, and possible deviations were tracked but not fully reported or analytically controlled, although session completion was high and no participant reportedly initiated psychotherapy during the study.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: However, participants were unblinded to the training they were undergoing, which is a complication inherent to the use of active controls.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only one of 24 enrolled participants withdrew, but the analysis used completers rather than retaining that participant and provided no outcome data or sensitivity analysis for the withdrawal; the potential impact is limited by the low attrition rate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Only one participant assigned to the HRVB group withdrew participation prior to completion of the study. Thus, the final sample included 12 participants in the LZNF group and 11 in the HRVB group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Key PTSD and anxiety outcomes were participant-reported by unblinded participants, and physiological recordings involved manual artifact removal with no report that assessors were blinded to intervention, allowing knowledge of treatment to influence both subjective and manually processed outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For each assessment, participants completed two self-report symptom questionnaires: the PTSD Checklist for DSM-V (PCL-5) and the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI).

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported despite seven outcomes and multiple analytic choices, and a favorable responder subgroup was defined post hoc by selecting LZNF participants who improved on the same neural outcome, creating substantial selective-reporting risk.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This subgroup consisted of participants in the LZNF group who showed any amount of decrease from Time 1 to Time 2 in the total number of significant CSD z-scores within the targeted networks.

overall_summary: Overall ROBINS-I risk is serious, driven by nonrandom alternating allocation with unadjusted baseline and co-intervention confounding, unblinded self-reported and manually processed outcomes, and selective-analysis concerns—especially the outcome-defined responder subgroup. Low attrition and clear intervention classification do not offset these serious domains.

design_rationale: Eligible participants were explicitly randomized between the interactive program and psycho-educational website using a computerized coin flip.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random mechanism was reported, but allocation concealment was not described and one notable baseline imbalance (severe force during the rape) was statistically significant.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomized to the interactive program or psycho-educational website based on a computerized coin flip.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew which distinct online program they received, adherence to the interactive program was low, and although an ITT analysis with multiple imputation was reported, prominent analyses also excluded non-initiators and participants without post-test data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analyses were conducted on individuals who initiated the assigned programs and provided data at post-test assessments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were missing for a substantial and differential proportion of randomized participants, particularly in the interactive arm, and only two of seven interactive-treatment dropouts provided post-treatment data, so missingness could plausibly bias the effect estimate despite multiple imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: It also should be noted that overall only 72.6% of individuals who initiated one of the two programs completed the post-treatment assessment, and thus it is not known whether these individuals who did not complete the assessment experienced clinical benefit.

domain_judgments.rationale: The PTSD outcome was measured with an established structured instrument in both groups, but outcome interviewers were explicitly not blinded and the symptom ratings could therefore have been influenced by knowledge of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Additionally, given the nature of the trial, individuals completing pre-, post- and follow-up assessments were not blind to participants’ intervention condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, while several outcomes, time points, completer and imputed ITT estimates, and moderator analyses were available, leaving scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To evaluate the comparative efficacy of the two programs, a residual difference score model was used to assess change from pre- to post-treatment.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because substantial, differential missing outcome data could bias the estimated intervention effect and outcome interviewers were not blinded to treatment assignment. Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment, imperfect adherence with mixed analysis populations, and lack of a reported preregistration or analysis plan.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 164 women were randomized before study procedures to standard care or the video intervention condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was described as randomized, but the sequence-generation and concealment methods were not reported, and there was a notable baseline imbalance in completed rape history (67.1% versus 46.8%).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: No differences were observed on these variables, except that more individuals in the SC condition reported a completed rape (67.1%) than those in the VI condition (46.8%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they viewed the video, no manipulation/adherence check was performed, and the available-case ANCOVAs were not intention-to-treat analyses, although no explicit intervention-related deviations were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: There was no manipulation check in the study; thus, we were unable to examine the extent to which the women attended to the information in the video, if they liked it, or what components of the video were influential, if at all.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for fewer than half of the 164 randomized participants at each follow-up, and the authors acknowledge that completers may differ from dropouts, with no analysis establishing that missingness was unrelated to outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 164 women randomized in the study, data from 69 participants at 2 weeks and 74 participants at 2 months were available for analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: The validated self-report outcome instruments were administered consistently by research assistants described as blind to study condition, but participants were aware of receiving the behavioral intervention and could therefore have reported subjective anxiety and PTSD symptoms differently.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Approximately 3 days after the SANE examination, trained research assistants, blind to the study condition, contacted the participants to introduce themselves and remind the participants of the 2-week assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Two hypotheses and several named outcomes and time points were specified, but no preregistration or prespecified analysis plan was reported, and the switch from a contemplated repeated-measures model to multiple ANCOVAs leaves scope for selective analysis and reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A repeated measures design was considered, but the power for the analyses was significantly impacted by sample attrition. Therefore... one-way analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was conducted on each of the distress measures.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because fewer than half of randomized participants contributed outcomes at either follow-up, and the possibility of outcome-related attrition was not excluded. Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation methods, lack of participant blinding/adherence verification, available-case analysis, and no reported preregistration.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that participants were randomly assigned to B-CBT or assessment control initially, with randomization later adjusted when supportive counseling was added.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment was reported, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not described, and assault type was substantially imbalanced across groups despite statistical adjustment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the start of the study, participants were randomly assigned to either four sessions weekly of B-CBT or AC; 1 year into the study, the SC condition was added, and randomization was adjusted accordingly to increase the probability of participants being assigned to the SC condition rather than either the AC or the B-CBT condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and therapists could not be blinded to these distinct behavioral interventions, and the primary reported efficacy analyses excluded 26.7% of randomized participants rather than using an appropriate intention-to-treat analysis; LOCF sensitivity analyses were inadequate and changed some findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Therefore, given our primary interest in testing the efficacy of a brief, four-session intervention, only data for completers will be presented here. All analyses also were conducted using the last observation carried forward method (LOCF), with preintervention scores for dropouts included in all analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were missing for a substantial proportion after 24 of 90 participants dropped out, and the reported complete-case results could be biased despite similar observed baseline characteristics and dropout rates; LOCF using baseline values does not establish robustness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twenty-four participants (26.7%) dropped out of the intervention, leaving 66 completers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated outcomes were assessed consistently and interviewer-rated outcomes used assessors described as blind, but key favorable findings involved self-reported PTSD and anxiety from participants who necessarily knew their assigned behavioral condition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Interviewers blind to treatment assignment conducted independent evaluations.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan was reported, while several outcomes, time points, pairwise contrasts, completer/LOCF approaches, and derived recovery outcomes allowed multiple eligible results to be selected.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because we had specific, directional hypotheses regarding the relative efficacy of the three interventions (B-CBT > AC; B-CBT > SC), we conducted planned comparisons to test these hypotheses.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by substantial missing outcome data and primary completer-only analyses rather than an appropriate intention-to-treat approach; some reported effects also disappeared under the LOCF sensitivity analysis. Additional concerns arise from insufficient detail on sequence generation/concealment, unblinded self-reported outcomes, and no reported prespecified analysis plan.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports computer-generated random assignment of 42 baseline-assessed participants to HIC or LIC by an independent third party.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated and assigned by an independent third party, with participants and research personnel blinded, and reported baseline differences were consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Individuals who completed all baseline assessments were randomly assigned to the HIC condition or the LIC condition based on a computer-generated random number system prior to attending the first training session. Conditions were assigned by an independent third party using computer software, so that participants and research personnel remained blind to subjects’ conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and personnel were reportedly blinded and the active interventions were similar, but attrition and protocol removals were substantial, while the purported ITT analysis used last observation carried forward rather than a robust missing-data approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: First, intent-to-treat (ITT) analyses were conducted on all randomized participants, with missing data imputed using the last observation carried forward (LOCF) method for individuals who did not complete the post-training assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Post-training outcomes were missing for half of randomized participants (21/42 completers), and the primary ITT analysis replaced missing outcomes with baseline values using LOCF, which does not establish that results were unbiased by missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The rate in the present study (40% of those randomized, 26% of those who began the intervention) is on the upper end of the published rates in prior research.

domain_judgments.rationale: PTSD symptoms were measured identically across groups with the validated clinician-administered CAPS, and participants and research personnel were reported to remain blinded to condition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Conditions were assigned by an independent third party using computer software, so that participants and research personnel remained blind to subjects’ conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration is identified and primary outcomes are named, but no protocol or prespecified analysis plan is presented for verification, while numerous outcomes, ITT/completer analyses, an outlier modification, and exploratory analyses create potential analytic flexibility.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The current study reports the results of a pilot randomized controlled trial of a computerbased proactive control training program in women with PTSD secondary to sexual trauma (clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT02139137).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because approximately half of randomized participants lacked post-training outcome data and missing outcomes were handled using LOCF, leaving a substantial risk that attrition biased the estimated effects. There are also some concerns about intervention-effect analysis and selective reporting, despite a sound randomization process and blinded, appropriate outcome measurement.

design_rationale: The study explicitly used a computerized random-number generator with stratified blocked randomization to assign participants in a 1:1:1 ratio to PPRS, PIRI, or TAU.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence generation was clearly random and analyzed groups were broadly balanced, but allocation concealment was described only for phase 2 and is unclear for the 28 phase-1 participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computerized random numbers generator was used to randomly assign participants to one of three conditions via a stratified blocked randomization procedure with variable block sizes of 9 or 12.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and administering nurses could know the visibly different intervention received, procedures changed between phases, and the efficacy analyses excluded all randomized participants without follow-up rather than using an intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A final limitation is that we included only participants who had at least one follow-up because we did not collect baseline substance use data; future studies should collect these data to conduct intent-to-treat analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 154 of 233 participants who completed their assigned condition contributed any follow-up data, with just 121 available at T3, and comparisons on condition, age, and minority status do not establish that missingness was unrelated to outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 233 participants, 154 (66%) completed one or more follow-up assessments (54 in PPRS, 48 in PIRI, 52 in TAU).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured consistently using self-report questions and validated AUDIT/DAST instruments by interviewers blinded to assignment, but participants necessarily knew whether they watched a video and potentially its content, which could influence subjective substance-use reports.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants completed up to three structured telephone follow-up interviews targeted at 1.5, 3, and 6 months post-SA conducted by Counseling Psychology doctoral students who were blind to study condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and multiplicity was acknowledged, but the full protocol was unavailable and numerous outcomes, time points, contrasts, moderators, and main-effect/interaction models left substantial scope for selective reporting; some additional comparison data were available only on request.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial is registered at clinicaltrials.gov under the registration number NCT01430624 and includes protocol information, although full protocol is not publicly available.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven principally by exclusion of roughly one-third of participants from all follow-up analyses, additional attrition by six months, and the absence of an intention-to-treat analysis. Unclear phase-1 concealment, participant knowledge of condition, self-reported outcomes, and substantial analytic flexibility add further concerns.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 64 participants were randomly assigned 1:1 using small-block randomization to SoC or SoC plus ImpACT, with assignments kept in sealed envelopes until assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Block randomization and sealed-envelope concealment were reported, but the exact sequence-generation method and whether envelopes were opaque, sequentially numbered, and tamper-proof were not described; additionally, several baseline PTSD scores differed between arms in this small trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to the standard of care control condition... or the experimental intervention condition... using a small block (size 8 or 10) randomization procedure. Condition assignments were placed in sealed envelopes, blinded to study staff until assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and staff were necessarily unblinded, intervention receipt was incomplete—especially for group sessions—and referrals or supportive contacts could affect outcomes, although primary outcomes were analyzed according to randomized assignment regardless of exposure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention conditions, neither participants nor staff could be blinded to condition assignment... For group sessions, attendance was poor, with only 25.0% receiving any group sessions... Participants were retained in these analyses regardless of intervention exposure, following an intent-to-treat analysis of the outcomes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were missing for a substantial proportion of the small randomized sample (only 45/64 at 3 months and 51/64 at 6 months), and loss to follow-up was associated with hazardous drinking and recent intimate-partner violence, factors plausibly related to psychological and adherence outcomes, without a convincing missingness sensitivity analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants lost to follow-up at the 6-month assessment were significantly more likely than those retained to have reported hazardous drinking (69.2% vs. 37.3%, p = 0.04) and recent physical intimate partner violence at baseline (46.2% vs. 17.65%, p = 0.03).

domain_judgments.rationale: Key psychological outcomes were interviewer-administered self-reports and adherence was partly self-reported; because participants and staff were unblinded and assessor blinding was not reported, outcome reports or assessments could plausibly be influenced by intervention knowledge, particularly for subjective outcomes targeted by the intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention conditions, neither participants nor staff could be blinded to condition assignment. Interviewer-administered assessments were conducted within a private room in the clinic and lasted approximately 90 minutes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was registered, the paper reports numerous PTSD totals/subscales, coping factors, adherence outcomes, time points, interaction models, clinically significant-change tests, and explicitly post-hoc exploratory analyses, with no prespecified analysis plan provided to establish that reported results were selected independently of findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Exploratory post-hoc analysis revealed that a significantly larger proportion of participants in the ImpACT arm compared to SoC had clinically significant reductions in total symptom severity scores from baseline to 3-month assessments.

overall_summary: Overall RoB 2 risk is high, driven by substantial and plausibly informative missing outcome data, unblinded measurement of subjective self-reported outcomes, and extensive exploratory/post-hoc analyses across multiple outcomes and time points. Some concerns also remain about incompletely described allocation concealment and incomplete intervention receipt.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomly assigned after baseline assessment by a research assistant using a virtual coin-toss program.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was generated using a virtual coin toss, but allocation concealment was not described and the small sample had notable baseline imbalances, including significantly greater dissociation in the wait-list group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After diagnostic assessment and completion of baseline outcome measures, a research assistant randomised participants to either trial condition using a virtual coin toss programme.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating clinicians could not be blinded, intervention delivery departed from protocol in session number and duration, ancillary practical support varied, and efficacy analyses used completers rather than intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Given that this was a feasibility study with only a small sample and some missing data, we analysed completer data rather than performing an intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Endline outcomes were unavailable for a substantial and differential fraction of randomized participants (13/15 NET completers versus 7/10 completing the waiting period, with only 5 wait-list participants represented in several analyses), and exclusions were related to pregnancy, treatment preference, suicidality, and health deterioration, all of which could be outcome-related.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In total, 13 participants completed NET, and seven completed the waiting period (and post-wait assessments).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although validated outcome instruments were used similarly across groups, assessor blinding failed in several cases, self-reported outcomes were susceptible to participants' knowledge of assignment, and nonstandard interpreter translation could have influenced measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Unblinding therefore occurred in several cases, either ‘accidentally’ (e.g. the assessor had encountered the participant attending for a therapy appointment) or because the participant made a disclosure during an assessment session, despite being asked not to do so.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and the primary construct was identified, but the article does not establish a prespecified statistical analysis plan and reports multiple measures and change definitions, leaving some scope for selective analysis or reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The main clinical outcome in the study was overall PTSD symptom severity, measured through a clinician-administered diagnostic assessment and a self-report scale.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by per-protocol/completer analysis with substantial and plausibly informative attrition, deviations from the intervention protocol and unequal ancillary support, and compromised assessor blinding. Randomization and selective reporting also raise some concerns because concealment was unclear, baseline imbalance occurred, and analysis prespecification was not demonstrated.
